preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == 2 * int(n) for n, s in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.strip())
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line is a binary string s of length 2n, where n is the integer given in the first line of the test case.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(n) <= 10**5 for n, _ in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.strip())
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is an integer (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) where 2n is the length of the binary string.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in s) for n, s in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.strip())
preconditions.description: The binary string s consists only of characters '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line := line.strip()) == '-1' or (len(stdout_line.split()) == 2 * int(n) + 1 and all(1 <= int(idx) <= 2 * int(n) for idx in stdout_line.split()[1:])) for n, _ in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.strip() and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)))
postconditions.description: For each test case, if no solution exists, the output is '-1'. Otherwise, the first line contains m (0 ≤ m ≤ 2n) followed by m distinct indices b_1, ..., b_m in increasing order, and the second line contains n distinct indices p_1, ..., p_n in increasing order.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line := line.strip()) != '-1' and (m := int(stdout_line.split()[0])) >= 0 and m <= 2 * int(n) and len(set(stdout_line.split()[1:])) == m and all(1 <= int(idx) <= 2 * int(n) for idx in stdout_line.split()[1:]) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (p_indices := [int(idx) for idx in line.split()]) and len(p_indices) == int(n) and len(set(p_indices)) == int(n) and all(1 <= idx <= 2 * int(n) for idx in p_indices) and sorted(p_indices) == p_indices for n, _ in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.strip() and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the first line contains m (0 ≤ m ≤ 2n) and m distinct indices b_1, ..., b_m in increasing order, and the second line contains n distinct indices p_1, ..., p_n in increasing order, where p_1, ..., p_n are the indices of the first subsequence s^p.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line := line.strip()) != '-1' and (m := int(stdout_line.split()[0])) >= 0 and m <= 2 * int(n) and (b_indices := [int(idx) for idx in stdout_line.split()[1:]]) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (p_indices := [int(idx) for idx in line.split()]) and (q_indices := [i for i in range(1, 2 * int(n) + 1) if i not in p_indices]) and (s := stdin.splitlines()[stdin.splitlines().index(line) + 1]) and (s_list := list(s)) and (s_rotated := s_list.copy()) and (all(s_rotated[b_indices[i]] == s_rotated[b_indices[i - 1]] if i > 0 else s_rotated[b_indices[i]] == s_rotated[b_indices[-1]] for i in range(len(b_indices))) if b_indices else True) and (all(s_rotated[b_indices[i]] == s_list[b_indices[(i - 1) % len(b_indices)]] for i in range(len(b_indices))) if b_indices else True) and (s_p := ''.join(s_rotated[p_idx - 1] for p_idx in p_indices)) == (s_q := ''.join(s_rotated[q_idx - 1] for q_idx in q_indices)) for n, s in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.strip() and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)) and (line := next((l for l in stdin.splitlines() if l.strip()), None)))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the output must satisfy that after rotating the subsequence defined by b_1, ..., b_m right by one position, the string s can be partitioned into two subsequences s^p and s^q of equal length n, where s^p is formed by the characters at indices p_1, ..., p_n and s^q is formed by the remaining characters, and s^p equals s^q.
